newsitem.title: USA: Nevada man dies in descent from Mount Rainier.
newsitem.headline: Nevada man dies in descent from Mount Rainier.

text.p: Mount Rainier claimed its first victim in nearly two years when a Nevada man fell to his death while descending from Washington state's highest peak, officials said Wednesday.

Don McIntyre, 51, of Reno died Tuesday when he and his climbing partner fell into a 50-foot (15 metre) crevasse at the 13,500-foot (4,050 metre) level, said John Krambrink, chief ranger at Mount Rainier National Park.
McIntyre's partner, Joel Koury, 37, of Santa Monica, Calif., suffered only minor injuries, Krambrink said.
The two men had climbed the 14,411-foot (4,323-meter) mountain by the difficult Liberty Ridge route on the north side and were descending Emmons Glacier when they fell.

Rescuers flown to the summit of the ice-covered dormant volcano on a military CH-214 helicopter were able to rescue Koury but could not recover McIntyre's body which was left at the lip of the crevasse.
Krambrink said he expected rangers would be able to recover the body sometime this week, although he said it was in an "extremely precarious position."

It was the first climbing fatality on the popular mountain since August 1995, when two Seattle-area men fell to their deaths. Krambrink said more than 8,000 people climb Mount Rainier annually, and up to half reach the summit.
